validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + core specs are solidly confirmed by THREE mutually independent trade-press/industry sources, none tracing to GEM or to each other: Natural Gas Intelligence (Mar. 2017, quotes an FERC docket number CP15-500 for the Presidio border crossing), Pipeline & Gas Journal (May 2017, 'Texas Pipeline Construction Projects Finished'), and the Offshore-Technology/Hydrocarbons-Technology project profile (industry database, formerly hydrocarbons-technology.com -- same URL now redirects to offshore-technology.com under a common template, still the same publisher/content). All three independently state: 148-mile length, 42-inch diameter, 1.4 Bcf/d (=1,400 MMcf/d) capacity, originates at the Waha Hub outside Fort Stockton (Pecos County) and ends at the Texas-Mexico border near Presidio -- an exact match to GEM's Length=148.00mi, Diameter=42.00in, Capacity=1400.00 MMcf/d, StartLocation=Fort Stockton, EndLocation=Presidio. All three also independently confirm in-service March 31, 2017 (matches StartYear1=2017) and that the pipeline is an operating natural-gas transmission trunk (matches Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission, Status=operating) -- it is regulated as a Texas RRC intrastate line for its onshore length but required a FERC presidential permit / Section 3 authorization (CP15-500 and related dockets) for the border crossing itself, which is why both FERC (Federal Register notices 2015-2016) and the Texas RRC (T-4 permit, verified at documentcloud.org/documents/2062745) have independent records of it. Existence is further corroborated by extensive contemporaneous opposition-group and news coverage (DeSmog Blog Jan. 2017, verified live) describing eminent-domain fights over this specific route -- this is not a GEM-only or invented entity. SegmentCost=767,000,000 USD is confirmed by the Offshore/Hydrocarbons-Technology profile ('The $767m pipeline...') and closely corroborated (within 0.1%) by an independent Texas Observer investigative piece quoting a landowner-advocacy economist citing 'a $766 million project' -- the $1M variance reads as an early estimate vs. final cost rounding difference, not a material conflict, so I am NOT flagging SegmentCost as a spec concern. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row Texas-operating roster: not a duplicate. Its sister ETP/Carso/MasTec export project, Comanche Trail Pipeline (P2519, 195 mi, 1.1 Bcf/d, Waha to San Elizario/El Paso), is confirmed by the same Pipeline & Gas Journal article to be a physically distinct pipeline with different length, capacity and route -- the two are commonly discussed together in press because they were built by the same consortium under the same CFE (Mexico) gas-export program, but they are not the same pipe. HARVESTED CITATION POOL: the wiki page listed 21 citations; I opened/verified 11 of them directly (SEC EDGAR MasTec 10-K Ex.21, Motley Fool, Offshore/Hydrocarbons-Technology, DocumentCloud T-4 permit, DeSmog Blog, Texas Observer via fresh search, plus resolving the bit.ly shortener to Energy Transfer's now-changed 'transpecospipelinefacts.com' microsite, which no longer carries the original numbers). Several original harvested URLs have rotted (naturalgasintel.com/articles/109845... and pgjonline.com/2017/05/03/... both now redirect/404 under the old path) -- I located the SAME articles live at their current URLs via search (naturalgasintel.com/news/texas-to-mexico-trans-pecos-pipeline-nearing-in-service/ and pgjonline.com/news/2017/05/texas-pipeline-construction-projects-finished) rather than treating the dead old links as evidence of anything. Not opened: fractracker.org map, carso.com.mx annual report (blocked 403 to curl but url_verifier context suggests it names Carso's 42-inch stake -- redundant with SEC data already used), ijglobal.com (paywalled transaction database), sobreorugas.com (Spanish construction-industry blog on Wahalajara system completion), dallasnews.com, truth-out.org, bigbendconservationalliance.org, sierraclub.org, ogj.com (2015 permitting-process piece), texasmonthly.com, fronterasdesk.org -- these are largely opposition/advocacy pieces on the eminent-domain fight, not additional spec sources, and existence/specs are already solidly corroborated without them.

validity.recommendation: correct Operator to 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC' (currently reads 'Texas Pecos Pipeline LLC')
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Operator value 'Texas Pecos Pipeline LLC' does not match the pipeline's actual legal operating entity in ANY source I could find. FOUR independent, mutually unrelated sources -- a federal regulator's own docket index (Federal Register, 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC; Notice of Application', verified live), a public-company SEC filing (MasTec, Inc. Form 10-K Exhibit 21 'List of Subsidiaries', which lists 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC (33% owned by MasTec TPP, LLC) (16% owned by Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC) (51% owned by Carso Energy Corp.)', verified live via a SEC-compliant User-Agent), an operator/permit directory (Buckhead Energy's Texas RRC operator profile page, titled 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC (Houston, TX)', verified live), and Energy Transfer's OWN investor-relations capacity-nomination portal (asset ticker 'TPP', page titled 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC - Energy Transfer', verified live) -- all independently spell the entity 'Trans-Pecos Pipeline, LLC'. None of them uses 'Texas Pecos'. This reads as a 'Texas'/'Trans-' name-corruption error (an easy one, since the pipeline is IN Texas), not a genuine alternate name for a different entity -- I found zero sources anywhere using 'Texas Pecos Pipeline'. Recommend the Operator cell be corrected.

validity.recommendation: re-verify ConstructionMonth (currently September/2016) -- independent sourcing points to Q1 2016, not September
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records ConstructionYear=2016, ConstructionMonth=9 (September). The one independent source I found that states a construction-start window -- the Offshore-Technology/Hydrocarbons-Technology project profile (verified live: 'Construction Started Q1 2016... Construction on the project began in the first quarter of 2016 and was completed in early 2017') -- puts the start in Q1 2016 (Jan-Mar), not September. A broader web search of trade coverage did not surface any source citing a September 2016 start date; several instead describe the project as already well into construction by mid-2016 (the T-4 operating permit was issued April 2015, and opposition/eminent-domain coverage describes active construction activity from spring 2016 onward). This is a material month-level discrepancy (Q1 vs Q3), not a rounding difference, so I am NOT proposing this as a confirmed ref -- flagging it as an open spec question for Update to resolve against a primary FERC/RRC notice-to-proceed record rather than guessing at the correct month myself.

Ownership is confirmed at high tier by TWO independent sources that agree exactly with GEM's percentages: MasTec, Inc.'s SEC Form 10-K Exhibit 21 (verified live, states the pipeline entity is '33% owned by MasTec TPP, LLC / 16% owned by Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC / 51% owned by Carso Energy Corp.') and an independent Motley Fool investing article from Dec. 2016 (verified live, states 'Energy Transfer only holds a 16% stake, whereas Mastec owns 33% and Carso controls 51%'). These match GEM's Owner1=ETP Legacy 16%, Owner2=Carso Energy 51%, Owner3=MasTec 33% exactly (percentages sum to 100%). Caveat: GEM's own label 'ETP Legacy' for Owner1 is GEM's internal naming convention for the pre-2018-merger Energy Transfer Partners entity (here specifically 'Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC' per the SEC filing) -- the underlying company and percentage are independently confirmed, the exact sub-entity name is not something I'm treating as a defect since it follows an established GEM convention used elsewhere in the tracker.
